newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Rosneft interested in Bulgaria oil refinery stake.
newsitem.headline: Rosneft interested in Bulgaria oil refinery stake.

text.p: Russia's state oil holding company Rosneft is interested in buying a stake in Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim, a Rosneft vice president said on Tuesday.
"Rosneft is interested in buying a stake in Neftochim," Favoris Davletyarov told reporters. He did not elaborate.
Bulgaria's interim government, which took office on February 13, said it would sell part of Neftochim but did not specify how big the stake would be.
Rosneft, which has a joint venture with Neftochim named Rosbulneft, plans to expand its activities on the Bulgarian market by opening petrol stations, Davletyarov said.
"We have already specified four pieces of land to start the construction of our filling stations and one of them is in Sofia," he said.
Devletyarov is in Sofia as a member of a Russian delegation headed by Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov.
Bulgaria and Russia on Tuesday signed a protocol on energy, trade and other issues, preparing the agenda for an intergovernmental committee meeting planned for June.
Russian private firm Elit is willing to buy Bulgaria's forklift truck producer Balkancar Holding, officials said.
Lobov and his Bulgarian counterpart Alexander Bozhkov said they had agreed on a scheme for liberalising trade between the two countries.
Under a protocol signed by Lobov and Bozhkov, a report by experts from the two countries suggesting how to ease bilateral trade should be finalised by the end of April, Bozhkov said.

"Before the intergovernmental committee meeting, which is expected to be held in June, an intergovernmental declaration will be signed for the liberalisation of bilateral trade," Bozhkov told a news conference before Lobov's departure.

He said Bulgarian firms were willing to participate in the reconstruction of ceramic plants in Russia, and the two sides were interested in setting up joint ventures in information technology, mining and aviation production.

Russia will also help Bulgaria upgrade all six reactors of the Kozloduy nuclear plant, and steps will be taken to solve problems related to signing an agreement for the transportation of fresh nuclear fuel from Russia to Bulgaria, officials said.
In March atomic experts from the two countries will renew negotiations on reprocessing Kozloduy's spent fuel in Russia and disposing of its waste there.
